title: Introduce 'Skip Intro' Button Across All Netflix Surfaces
description:
Implement a public-facing 'Skip Intro' button on the video player UI across all Netflix platforms globally — web, iOS, Android, Smart TV, and set-top boxes. The button will appear dynamically exactly when the opening credits sequence begins for a television series and will vanish immediately when the sequence ends. Clicking the button advances the playhead instantly to the exact millisecond the post-credit scene starts. The feature requires a new metadata pipeline where audio fingerprinting and machine learning models scan the entire Netflix catalog to mathematically identify the exact start and end timestamps of intro sequences for every episode.

Timeline:
- Early 2017: Internal hackathon prototype and manual tagging of 250 shows.
- March 2017: Initial silent launch on the Web player for select TV series.
- August 2017: Official rollout on television applications (Smart TVs, consoles).
- May 2018: Deployment on mobile platforms (iOS and Android).

Internal experiment data (as cited in Netflix Tech Blog):
- Manual fast-forwarding data reveals approximately 15% of subscribers are manually seeking past the first five minutes of episodes.
- A/B testing on the web prototype showed massive user engagement with the button, reducing time-to-content friction to zero.
- Binge-watching continuity increased measurably in cohorts with the button compared to the control group.

Stated rationale:
1. Eliminate manual fast-forward friction, which is imprecise on remotes and frustrating for binge-watchers.
2. Respect the viewer's time by giving them total control over their immersion experience.
3. Solidify Netflix as the most user-centric streaming platform, prioritizing consumer convenience over creator vanity or traditional TV norms.

Scope of change:
- All video player UIs across all clients (Web, Smart TVs, iOS, Android, Apple TV, Roku)
- New backend ML pipeline (Audio Fingerprinting) to detect intro timestamps at scale.
- New CMS metadata fields for 'intro_start' and 'intro_end' timestamps per episode.
target_users: All 110 million global Netflix subscribers who watch serialized television content on the platform.
affected_domains: Video Player UI (Web, iOS, Android, TV, Consoles)
priority: P1 — Core Viewing Experience / User Delight
decision_maker: Netflix Director of Product Innovation, UX Design Team
